cards.explanation: The answer is birds. Jesus says some seed fell along the path, and “…the birds came and devoured it.” The seed was out in the open on that path, and the birds took it. Sown and swallowed in one verse is the fastest turnaround I've ever seen from a seed, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, “It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.” Quick, not slow. That seed was in a hurry, and I think a hurried start is worth remembering as the story goes on, friends.

The answer is that they had no root. Jesus says, “But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.” The seed sprang up quickly, but nothing was holding it below. I know the feeling of looking sharp and being shaky underneath, friends.
The answer is choke. The thorns “…grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.” That is a rough neighborhood for a seedling, friends. It never even gets to produce a crop.

The answer is True, and it's a relief after three rough landings. On the good soil the seed “…sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop…” Three steps, and this seed makes every one of them. Finally some good news in the field, friends.

The answer is the parable He just told. Verse 10 says that as soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about it. They had a question and they asked it, which is always the smart move, friends.

The answer is the mystery of the kingdom of God. Verse 11: “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you…” That's what Jesus says to the Twelve and those around Him. Then comes the other side, that to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables. I know what it's like to be handed something I never expected, like a whole bakery after years in a junk drawer.

The answer is that they might turn and be forgiven. The line is “otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.” It comes right after the words about ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding. I'll be honest, friends, this is one of the weightier verses in the chapter. I'd read it slowly.

The answer is that Satan comes and takes the word away. Jesus says, “As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.” Notice the words “As soon as…” That is quick work, friends.

The answer is trouble or persecution over the word. Jesus says, “When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.” They received it with joy, but they have no root. Joy at the start, no root underneath, friends.

The answer is False. The verse says that when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, “…they quickly fall away.” That's fast, not many years. It also says they remain for only a season, which fits, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, “…and it becomes unfruitful.” That matches the thorn seedlings in verse 7, which yielded no crop. Same ending, now with the meaning spelled out, friends.

The answer is that they receive it and produce a crop. Jesus says so in verse 20, with a crop of thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold. The rocky-ground people received it too, but these ones go on to produce a crop, friends.
The answer is stand. Jesus asks, “Doesn’t he set it on a stand?” Nobody lights a lamp and then tucks it under a basket or a bed. A lamp belongs up where it can do its job, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.” He says it right after the lamp. So nothing concealed stays hidden forever, friends.

The answer is that even more will be added to you. Jesus says, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.” It's a generous verse, friends, and it starts with paying attention.

The answer is that even what he has will be taken away. Verse 25 says, “For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” That's a hard line, friends. I think it's the kind of saying that makes you slow down and read it again, so go ahead.
The answer is False. The verse says the seed sprouts and grows “…though he knows not how.” The man sleeps and wakes, and the seed keeps going. I bet that man sleeps better than I do, friends.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “All by itself the earth produces a crop…” In this parable the man scatters the seed, and the earth does the producing. Stalk, head, grain, all by itself, friends.
The answer is stalk, then head, then grain. Jesus says, “…first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.” There's no skipping ahead in that line, friends. Everything in its turn.
The answer is sickle. Jesus says, “…he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come.” As soon as the grain is ripe, the man gets to work. Good timing from a good farmer, friends.
The answer is True. Jesus says the mustard seed “…is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.” That is one tiny seed, friends. Keep that in mind for the very next verse.

The answer is the largest of all garden plants. Jesus says, “…it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches…” From the smallest seed to the largest plant, friends. That is some glow-up.

The answer is False. Jesus says it puts forth great branches “…so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.” Birds, not cattle of the field. Those cows would have to look elsewhere for shade, friends.

The answer is that He explains everything to them. Verse 34 says He did not tell the crowd anything without a parable, “But privately He explained everything to His own disciples.” Private lessons, friends. I'd have signed up.
